title: Hollow roots

objectives.can: Recognise forms of roots with ו or י in the middle and restore the root.

explanation.summary: In a hollow root the middle consonant is ו (rarely י), and in most forms it is not heard as a consonant: only a long vowel stands between the first and the last consonant. That is why these verbs seem to have two root letters in the Qal. The dictionary lists them by the infinitive, which shows the middle letter: קוּם, בּוֹא, שׁוּב.

sections.heading: Two letters and a long vowel
body: A regular verb has three consonants with short vowels between them. A hollow root keeps the first and the last consonant and puts a long vowel in the middle. The third masculine singular qatal of 'rise' is קָם, of 'come' it is בָּא, of 'return' it is שָׁב. The vowel is a qamets in these, and ē in the qatal of 'die', מֵת.

The middle letter does not appear in these forms, but the root has it. The infinitive construct shows it: לָבוֹא, 'to come', לָמוּת, 'to die', and לָשׂוּם. The infinitive absolute of 'die', מוֹת, is the same. For this reason lexica, and this library, name the root by a form like this: קוּם, בּוֹא, שׁוּב, מוּת, שׂוּם, סוּר, רוּם, נוּחַ, רוּץ, כּוּן, גּוּר. Other lists give the qatal, קָם and so on; the two are not different roots.

sections.heading: Qal: qatal, participle, yiqtol
body: The Qal qatal has qamets in the third persons (בָּאוּ) and a short vowel in the first and second: קַמְתִּי, בָּאתִי. The Qal yiqtol has a long vowel in the stem and a qamets under the prefix: יָקוּם, יָבוֹא, יָמוּת, תָּמוּת, יָסוּר. The imperative is the stem alone: קוּם, קוּמָה, קוּמוּ, קוּמִי, בֹּא, בֹּאוּ, שִׂים, סוּרוּ.

In the wayyiqtol and the jussive the stem vowel is shortened: וַיָּקָם from יָקוּם, וַיָּבֹא from יָבוֹא, וַיָּשָׁב from יָשׁוּב, וַיָּמָת and וַיָּמֹת, וַיָּשֶׂם from the root שׂוּם. The shortening is the same one you saw in other short forms of the yiqtol. The qamets under the prefix is what separates these from the first-waw verbs of the last lesson: וַיָּשָׁב is 'and he returned' (שׁוּב), while וַיֵּשֶׁב, with ē, is 'and he sat' (יָשַׁב).

sections.heading: Qatal or participle?
body: The third masculine singular qatal and the masculine singular participle of these verbs are spelled alike: בָּא, קָם, מֵת, שָׁב. Neither the consonants nor the vowels tell them apart. The stress can differ in the pointing, but a reader has to decide from the sentence. A form after הִנֵּה, or one that names what someone is doing, is usually a participle; a form in a story, with a past sense, is a qatal. The plurals are not ambiguous: the qatal is בָּאוּ and the participle is בָּאִים.
The feminine singular has the same problem, בָּאָה, whether qatal or participle.

sections.heading: Hiphil, Hophal and Niphal
body: In the Hiphil a ī stands in the stem, before the last consonant, and the prefix is הֵ or יָ: הֵקִים and יָקִים from קוּם, הֵבִיא and מֵבִיא and לְהָבִיא from בּוֹא, הֵסִיר from סוּר, הֵרִים from רוּם. The Hiphil wayyiqtol is shortened: וַיָּבֵא and וַיָּקֶם. The Hiphil weqatal of קוּם, וַהֲקִמֹתִי, has a long ô between the second and the third consonant when an ending is added, as in וְהֵבֵאתִי from בּוֹא.

The Hophal appears in יוּמָת, 'he shall be put to death'. The Niphal participle of כּוּן, נָכוֹן, means 'established, ready'. The mark of the hollow root in each is that the Qal-like long vowel stands where a regular verb has a consonant.

sections.heading: Restoring the root
body: Ask three questions. Does the form have only two consonants with a long vowel between them, where the context is a verb? Then the root may be hollow. Is the form a Hiphil with ī before the last consonant and a hē or yod-prefix with a long vowel? Then the same is true. And is the infinitive or the yiqtol available, with ו in the middle? Then put that ו between the two consonants you have. Check the result against the verse.

misunderstandings: A hollow root is not a root with two consonants. It has three; the middle one is a weak ו or י that has been absorbed into a long vowel.
The qatal and the participle of the same verb are not different words when they look alike. A third masculine singular such as בָּא can be either, and only the sentence tells which.
The shortened wayyiqtol וַיָּקָם is not a qatal; it is a wayyiqtol, and what looks like a qatal vowel is the shortened yiqtol stem.
וַיָּשָׁב and וַיֵּשֶׁב must not be confused: the first belongs to שׁוּב and the second to יָשַׁב.

deeper.heading: Roots with י in the middle
body: Roots with י in the middle form a smaller group; the corpus has the infinitive absolute of the verb 'understand' in one place only, so this lesson teaches the pattern of roots with ו. The principle is the same for both: a weak middle letter is reduced to a long vowel.
